subject: Medisphere private cluster — throughput cliff and 503s (exec signal)
messages:
From: Sam Thurman <sam@medisphere.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: alyssa.ops@medisphere.com
Date: Tue, 02 Oct 2028 08:23:00 -0700
Subject: Prod incident: private cluster throughput cliff, 503s starting ~07:45 PDT

Laura / Marissa —

We started seeing a sharp throughput cliff and a spike in 503 responses from our private VPC cluster in us-west-2 starting ~07:45 PDT. Key observations: p50 ~180ms (ok), p95 jumped from 320ms -> 1.6s, p99 ~4.2s. Approximately 18% of requests returned 503 within the first 30 minutes. Concurrent inflight requests plateaued while queue depth increased (worker queue compaction).

This began immediately after we applied a kernel patch (kernel 1.12.7) and a small model variant rollout (redwood-quant-v2) at 07:30. The cluster is on the dedicated on-prem bundle you manage; we saw significant KV cache evictions and long GC pauses in the attached logs.

We attached: logs_20281002.tar.gz (system+runtime logs), perf_snapshot_20281002.csv (sampled latencies + token counts).

This is impacting our customer-facing SLA for inference. Can your team confirm receipt and provide immediate mitigation steps and an ETA? We need executive transparency — our CTO and operations lead are on standby.

Sam
Sam Thurman
Head of SRE, Medisphere
attachments: logs_20281002.tar.gz (text), perf_snapshot_20281002.csv (csv)
From: laura_bennett@redwood.com <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Sam Thurman <sam@medisphere.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 02 Oct 2028 09:05:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Prod incident: private cluster throughput cliff, 503s starting ~07:45 PDT

Sam — thanks for the details and the attachments. We received the logs and snapshot. Our immediate priorities are: (1) stop the damage to customer requests, (2) collect targeted traces to narrow root cause, (3) provide a short remediation and exec note.

Immediate mitigation (we're initiating now):
- Irene (SRE) to drain canary nodes and put the affected pool into maintenance.
- Revert kernel 1.12.7 on one canary rack if there is no perf improvement within 30m of the drain.
- Route a portion of traffic to a pre-quantized model variant (redwood-legacy-fp16) to remove quantization/regression as a variable.
- Increase request concurrency throttle on the private adapter to reduce queue saturation (temporary).

Irene — please confirm you can start node drains and share ETA. Jonas — can you review for a possible emergency rollback if drains don't recover p95 by 30% in the next 45 minutes?

Sam — I will provide an exec note for your CTO and our leadership within 45 minutes. We'll open SUP-2028-849 and share the runbook link.

Laura Bennett
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference
attachments: runbook_v2.pdf (pdf)
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, irene_choi@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 02 Oct 2028 09:30:45 -0700
Subject: Re: Prod incident: private cluster throughput cliff, 503s starting ~07:45 PDT

Picking up here — quick action plan and ownership: 
1) Irene (owner): drain 2 nodes from the affected pool, run canary on revert image (rollback-kernel-1.12.6) on those nodes, validate p95/p99 and token throughput.
2) SRE: temporarily bump application-level batch size from 4 -> 8 to reduce per-request kernel context switching and amortize KV cache misses (monitor CPU).
3) Infra: increase middleware concurrency cap to drop queued requests earlier (fail fast) to protect tail latency.
4) If canary fails, full rollback of kernel across pool and emergency hotpatch for KV cache eviction policy.

Exec ask: Marissa / Laura please notify Medisphere execs that we have a recovery action in motion; if we do not see measurable improvement in 45 minutes, I will request an escalation call with Redwood CTO and Medisphere CTO. Also prepare a temporary credit proposal for SLA breach (Marissa).

Links: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SUP-2028-849 (ticket), https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-medisphere-runbooks (runbook).

Jonas Weber
VP Engineering, Redwood Inference
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, Sam Thurman <sam@medisphere.com>
Date: Tue, 02 Oct 2028 10:08:03 -0700
Subject: Re: Prod incident: private cluster throughput cliff, 503s starting ~07:45 PDT

Starting actions now:
- Draining node: rack-7-node-03 and rack-9-node-01 (expected drain time ~9–12 min each).
- Canary: booting rollback-kernel-1.12.6 image on rack-7-node-03; will route 5% of traffic for 10m then 20% if green.
- Observed in the logs: heavy KV cache churn plus increased worker process context-switches around the exact time of the kernel upgrade. Kernel 1.12.7 appears to change timer coalescing parameters affecting our polling cadence; this exacerbates small-batch inefficiencies in the model runtime.
- Short-term tuning: increasing batch size to 8 and enabling aggressive prefix caching for identical prompt prefixes. We'll watch CPU and GC.

If the canary recovers p95 by >30% within 30 minutes, we'll roll the revert across the pool. If not, execute plan B (full rollback + hotpatch).

Irene Choi
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference
